summary: The UK uses QNH (altitude above sea level), QFE (height above aerodrome), regional pressure setting (the lowest forecast pressure in a region) and standard 1013 hPa (flight levels). One hPa is about 30 ft (27 ft more precisely). The transition altitude is normally 3,000 ft outside controlled airspace and 5,000 or 6,000 ft within and below it, and the transition level must be at least 1,000 ft above it. The RPS usually reads low. Built from the Skyway Code pp.90-91.
src: The Skyway Code (CAP 1535 v4, Nov 2023), pp.90-91
sections: QNH: altitude above mean sea level. On the ground it reads aerodrome elevation
QFE: height above aerodrome level. On the ground it reads zero

Regional pressure setting (RPS): the lowest forecast pressure in an altimeter setting region. The UK has 21 regions with geographic names such as Portland or Cotswold. It normally gives a lower reading than actual altitude
Standard 1013 hPa: used above the transition altitude, giving flight levels and pressure altitude
1 hPa is about 30 ft (27 ft more precisely)
TA is the altitude above which position is given as a flight level
Outside CAS the UK transition altitude is normally 3,000 ft AMSL. Within and below CAS it is normally 5,000 or 6,000 ft (see ENR 1.7)
It is not mandatory for VFR flights in the UK to change to FLs, but it is for IFR
The lowest VFR flight level is normally FL35. The transition level is always at least 1,000 ft above the TA
Example: QNH 1000 and 3,000 ft altitude: set 1013 and the altimeter reads about 3,390 ft (13 hPa x 30 ft; 3,351 ft using 27 ft)
Use the most relevant QNH for your route or area. Use the RPS only if no local QNH is available
When transiting below or near CAS defined by altitude, use the QNH applicable to the airspace
When near CAS defined by flight level, use 1013 hPa
Larger aerodromes use QNH for take-off and landing

sum.Four pressure settings: QNH, QFE, RPS and 1013, and 30 ft per hPa (27 ft more precisely).
sum.Transition altitude and level: 3,000 ft outside CAS, 5,000 or 6,000 ft in and below CAS.
sum.Recommended procedure: Use the local QNH and 1013 near flight-level airspace.
